titleStmt.title: Task-phase-specific dynamics of basal forebrain neuronal ensembles

bibl.title: Task-phase-specific dynamics of basal forebrain neuronal ensembles

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: Among the full population of BF neurons, multiple distinct and complex forms of task-phase-specific activity are realized, forming unique population firing patterns for all task phases.

span.label: task-phase-specific firing in basal forebrain ensembles
span.quote: The current study examined the spiking activity of basal forebrain neuron populations across multiple phases of a selective attention task, addressing, in particular, the issue of complexity in ensemble firing patterns across time.

span.label: electrophysiology
span.quote: In the present work, large ensemble recordings of BF neurons were obtained during performance of a selective attention task with the goal of filling, to some extent, this gap in knowledge.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Anatomical organisation of local interconnections and of extrinsic afferents partitions basal forebrain neurons into distinct groups, which is why firing patterns cluster and why pair-wise trial-to-trial variability tracks pattern similarity.
span.quote: The foregoing results suggest that, for complex behavioral tasks, BF neurons are organized into distinct groups by virtue of the anatomical organization of their local interconnections, by their extrinsic afferents, or both.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Whichever subset of basal forebrain neurons is active at a given moment raises responsiveness specifically in the cortical targets those neurons reach, so task-phase-specific firing produces task-phase-specific cortical modulation.
span.quote: currently active set of BF neurons yields enhanced responsiveness among the subset of efferent targets reached by those neurons.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Simultaneous peaks and troughs in GABAergic and glutamatergic basal forebrain neurons could amplify inhibition of the cortical target, because GABAergic drive rises while excitatory glutamatergic drive is withdrawn.
span.quote: In an admittedly simplistic scenario, for instance, GABA and glutamate neurons could reach simultaneous peaks and troughs in activity, yielding amplification of GABAergic inhibition through coincident disfacilitation of excitatory glutamatergic input.

span.label: Recording sites could not be assigned to ventral pallidum versus substantia innominata, so the two sub-regions could not be analysed separately.
span.quote: The spread of electrodes within an array rendered it difficult to clearly determine which individual stereotrodes were within vental pallidum vs. substantia innominata and so separate analyses of spiking activity within these structures was not possible.

span.label: The neurochemical identity and cortical targets of the recorded neurons are unknown, limiting interpretation of the oppositely-tuned sub-groups.
span.quote: Given that the neurochemical identity and precise cortical targets of any single BF neuron in the present dataset are unknown, it is difficult to pinpoint the neurophysiological implications of BF sub-groups having opposite firing patterns.

span.label: The same task-phase signature appears in a second region, so it is not specific to the structure studied.
span.quote: An analogous set of task-phase-specific firing patterns was also observed in a population of posterior parietal cortex neurons

span.label: The categories are outputs of a clustering method, and their number is given only as large.
span.quote: Clustering techniques applied to the full population revealed a large number of distinct categories of task-phase-specific activity patterns

span.label: task phase
span.quote: Unique population firing-rate vectors defined each task phase and most categories of task-phase-specific firing had counterparts with opposing firing patterns

span.label: population firing-rate vectors
span.quote: Unique population firing-rate vectors defined each task phase and most categories of task-phase-specific firing had counterparts with opposing firing patterns

span.label: posterior parietal cortex
span.quote: An analogous set of task-phase-specific firing patterns was also observed in a population of posterior parietal cortex neurons

span.label: Clustering techniques
span.quote: Clustering techniques applied to the full population revealed a large number of distinct categories of task-phase-specific activity patterns

span.label: task-phase-specific firing patterns
span.quote: An analogous set of task-phase-specific firing patterns was also observed in a population of posterior parietal cortex neurons

span.label: a task phase - DEFINED BY A POPULATION FIRING-RATE VECTOR: each phase is identified by a unique vector across the recorded population, and most categories of task-phase-specific firing are said to have counterparts with opposing patterns, so a 'phase' here is a point in population activity space and its complement
span.quote: Unique population firing-rate vectors defined each task phase and most categories of task-phase-specific firing had counterparts with opposing firing patterns

span.label: the basal forebrain signature - ALSO PRESENT IN PARIETAL CORTEX: an analogous set of task-phase-specific firing patterns was observed in posterior parietal cortex neurons, so the pattern is not diagnostic of the structure the title names
span.quote: An analogous set of task-phase-specific firing patterns was also observed in a population of posterior parietal cortex neurons

span.label: a category of task-phase-specific activity - AN OUTPUT OF CLUSTERING: the distinct categories were revealed by clustering techniques applied to the full population, and the abstract gives their number as 'a large number', so the entities are individuated by the method rather than counted
span.quote: Clustering techniques applied to the full population revealed a large number of distinct categories of task-phase-specific activity patterns

span.label: builds-on → Golmayo et al., 2003
span.quote: The model is consistent with experimental work demonstrating that different sub-regions of prefrontal cortex can activate different BF neuron sub-groups which, in turn, can differentially impact responsiveness in primary somatosensory and visual cortices ( Golmayo et al., 2003).

span.label: builds-on → Gill et al., 2000
span.quote: Both possibilities are supported by work showing that neurons of the prelimbic subregion of prefrontal cortex exhibit activity correlates to all phases of a task requiring stimulus detection and choice of an instrumental response, and that such activity correlates are strongly dependent on BF efferents (Gill et al., 2000).

span.label: extends → Wilson and Rolls, 1990a,b; Tindell et al., 2004; Lin and Nicolelis, 2008
span.quote: BF neurons having dual responses to relevant light flashes or auditory tones as well as reward delivery have previously been observed ( Wilson and Rolls, 1990a,b; Tindell et al., 2004; Lin and Nicolelis, 2008 ).

span.label: task phase —operationalised-as→ population firing-rate vectors
span.quote: Unique population firing-rate vectors defined each task phase and most categories of task-phase-specific firing had counterparts with opposing firing patterns

span.label: t-test
span.quote: T-tests (alpha set at 0.01) were then performed, comparing the cross-trial firing rates for each neuron at each task phase

span.label: correlation
span.quote: a Pearson correlation was calculated for pairs of these vectors for all simultaneously recorded neurons

span.label: bootstrap
span.quote: For comparison, a boot-strapped control was generated for each neuron pair by randomly shuffling trial orders for one neuron of a pair to determine the mean noise correlation expected by chance (N = 100 randomizations).

span.label: principal components analysis
span.quote: The first eight principal components were utilized for clustering and explained 93% of the variability in taskphase-specific firing patterns

span.label: k-means clustering
span.quote: (2) initialization of clusters with K-means (500 restarts, K = 60); and (3) refinement of clusters according to a Gaussian mixture model wherein the full covariance matrix in the reduced space was utilized.

span.label: Gaussian mixture model
span.quote: (2) initialization of clusters with K-means (500 restarts, K = 60); and (3) refinement of clusters according to a Gaussian mixture model wherein the full covariance matrix in the reduced space was utilized.

span.label: standard deviation
span.quote: the mean absolute value of noise correlation was 0.10 ± 0.05 (STD) for same-stereotrode pairs and 0.11 ± 0.06 for different-stereotrode pairs

span.label: Distinct sub-populations of basal forebrain neurons reached their peak firing rate at every phase of the task, including the pure locomotion period between nose-poke and return to the arena centre, not only at stimulus onset and reward.
span.quote: First, distinct subsets of BF neurons reach peak activity at each task phase, including, for example, the time period directly between nose-poke and return to the center plate.

span.label: Nearly every category of task-phase-specific firing had a mirror-image counterpart category whose mean firing pattern was strongly negatively correlated with it, so at each task phase one group of neurons peaked while another fell to a trough.
span.quote: The mean task-phase-specific firing pattern for nearly every grouping of BF neurons has a counterpart in another grouping for which the mean task-phase-specific pattern is strongly negatively correlated

span.label: Apart from persistence before the light flash and after reward, no basal forebrain ensemble firing pattern recurred at a later task phase, so each task phase was marked by its own distinct population firing vector.
span.quote: While persistence in BF ensemble firing patterns is found over the time period preceding light flash onset and after reward obtainment, further evidence for pattern recurrence is not found, directly evidencing the fact that BF networks are capable of generating a large repertoire of distinct firing patterns.

span.label: Posterior parietal cortex neurons, clustered independently by the same algorithm, produced groups that each had both a strongly matching and a strongly opposing basal forebrain counterpart pattern.
span.quote: Remarkably, despite independence in the application of the algorithm to the BF and PPC populations, mean rate vectors for nearly all PPC groups had BF counterparts with highly similar and highly dissimilar patterns.

span.label: Neuron pairs whose mean firing patterns were similar also co-varied trial by trial: 62% of the 14,020 positively signal-correlated pairs had noise correlations at least two standard deviations above chance.
span.quote: Across 14,020 pairs having positive signal correlations, 62% exhibited noise correlation values two standard deviations or more greater than that expected by chance.

span.label: Most firing peaks (82.8%) and most firing troughs (62.2%) were statistically significant against a randomized-light-time control, and a third of all neuron-by-phase mean rates were significant, far above the 1% expected.
span.quote: Across all neurons and task phases, fully 33.8% of the observed mean firing rates yielded significance, a value far above that expected (1%) as well as that observed (1.02%) for the same set of comparisons for two separate randomizations

span.label: During the anticipatory period before the light flash — when attention to the visual field should be highest — basal forebrain mean firing was at its lowest and few neurons peaked, arguing against a role confined to anticipatory attention.
span.quote: Among the full population of BF neurons, mean activity rates were actually lowest during this time period, and associated with peak activity in only a few neurons.

span.label: The largest proportion of neurons peaked, and population mean rate was highest, in the period just after the light flash, pointing to a basal forebrain role in initiating and maintaining responses to relevant stimuli.
span.quote: Instead, the time period just after light flash was associated with peak firing in the largest proportion of neurons as well as the highest mean rate across the full population.

span.label: "signal" correlation
span.quote: “Signal” correlation is defined as the Pearson correlation between the mean, cross-phase firing rate vectors for any two neurons.

span.label: "noise" correlation
span.quote: Noise correlation determines, for any two neurons, the extent of any relation between their respective deviations from mean firing rates on each trial

span.label: time normalization (of trial epochs)
span.quote: Time normalization was accomplished by identifying the average time between light flash to nose-poke, nose-poke to center return, and center return to stop/reward across all trials and animals.

span.label: spatial location of the light flash (drawn from one of two probability distributions)
span.term: spatial location of the light flash (drawn from one of two probability distributions)
span.quote: The spatial position of a light flash for any given trial was randomly selected from one of two probability distributions

span.label: task-phase-specific mean firing rate
span.quote: Mean firing rate vectors were calculated for each cell on each recording day across all trials and for each bin of normalized time.

span.label: accuracy of identifying the light source
span.term: accuracy of identifying the light source
span.quote: Specifically, the spatial locations of lower-probability lights were less likely to be correctly identified

span.label: trial outcome (only rewarded/correct trials analysed)
span.quote: All data and analyses presented are based solely on rewarded trials (i.e., those associated with choice of the correct light source).

span.label: run trajectory (only ballistic direct runs retained, to hold epoch duration variability low)
span.term: run trajectory (only ballistic direct runs retained, to hold epoch duration variability low)
span.quote: rials in which the animal did not make ballistic, direct runs to and from the site of a nose-poke were not included so that trial-to-trial variability in task epoch durations were kept minimal relative to task epoch mean durations.

span.label: N = 1428 — basal forebrain neurons recorded, across 74 recording sessions
span.quote: activity dynamics of basal forebrain neurons ( N = 1428 from 74 recordings, see Figure 2) were recorded.

span.label: N = 203 — posterior parietal cortex neurons recorded during the same task
span.quote: a population of posterior parietal cortex (PPC) neurons (N = 203) recorded during performance of the same task, exhibited many of the same complex response fields as their BF counterparts

span.label: 33.8% — proportion of all neuron-by-task-phase mean firing rates that were statistically significant, against 1% expected by chance
span.quote: Across all neurons and task phases, fully 33.8% of the observed mean firing rates yielded significance, a value far above that expected (1%) as well as that observed (1.02%) for the same set of comparisons for two separate randomizations

span.label: 82.8 and 62.2% — proportions of firing peaks and firing troughs respectively that reached significance
span.quote: Across all neurons, 82.8 and 62.2% of peak and trough firing rates, respectively, reached statistical significance.

span.label: 53 of the 60 groups (88%) — share of firing-pattern categories that had an opposing counterpart category correlated below -0.5
span.quote: 53 of the 60 groups (88%) had counterparts for which the mean firing pattern among its members bore a correlation more negative than ( −0.5).

span.label: 0.81 (±0.07) and −0.78 (±0.10) — mean best positive and best negative correlation between each PPC category and its closest basal forebrain category
span.quote: the mean positive correlation across all groups was 0.81 ( ±0.07 STD) and the mean negative correlation −0.78 (±0.10 STD).

span.label: 62% of 14,020 pairs — positively signal-correlated neuron pairs whose noise correlation exceeded chance by two or more standard deviations
span.quote: Across 14,020 pairs having positive signal correlations, 62% exhibited noise correlation values two standard deviations or more greater than that expected by chance.

span.label: mean 70 ± 13% — daily behavioural success rate across the analysed recording sessions (range 26-93%)
span.quote: However, daily success rates ranged from 26 to 93% for the recording sessions analyzed in the present dataset (mean 70 ± 13%, see Supplemental Figure 2).

span.label: Eight — adult male Long-Evans rats used as subjects
span.quote: Eight adult, male Long-Evans rats served as behavioral subjects.
